name: shoutrrr-ccf81390-blind30-ots
instr:
# Shoutrrr delivers wrong notifications everywhere — diagnosing 30 faults without a test suite

A tool for pushing notifications out to chat rooms, mailboxes, paging desks and phones — driven either from a terminal or through library calls — now gets a great many of its destinations wrong. Nothing about the remote platforms changed and nothing about the calling programs changed; the same addresses and the same messages that used to go through cleanly now misbehave. Everything below was seen in ordinary use, and none of it needed unusual input. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Delivering one message and being told it failed, for a message that plainly arrived, is the loudest of the damage. The room-based chat product of the large web-search company answers with a plain success status and the message shows up in the room, yet the caller gets back an error quoting that answer. The corporate chat product of the big office-suite company, the one whose address is assembled from several long identifier segments, does the same: the post goes through and an error is raised anyway. Handing mail to a server that accepts the whole conversation ends in a returned error rather than a clean delivery. Firing an automation trigger by event name together with the extra data that rides along reports that the notification could not be delivered, although the trigger fires.
